At Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.




OUR PRODUCT

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 7,500 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.



Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.




AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.




ABOUT THE MANAGER, PRODUCT SUPPORT ROLE

Product Support is the front door to Float for thousands of Canadian businesses, and it is one of the strongest sources of product insight we have. We're looking for a Manager to own that function: its people, its quality, its operations and its impact on customers.



As part of our Product team, you will lead a team of Product Support Associates and Specialists, set the strategy and standards for how Float supports its customers, and make sure support scales with the business. You will be accountable for team results (SLAs, quality, CSAT and efficiency) and you will have real influence on the roadmap, our tooling and our AI-first approach to support.



This role reports to the functional leader of the Product Support team. You will have full ownership of people management for your team, including hiring, performance management, compensation input, and career development. You will stay close enough to customers and the queue to lead credibly, particularly during escalations and incidents.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


LEAD AND DEVELOP A HIGH-PERFORMING TEAM

 - Own people management for the Product Support team: hiring, onboarding, 1:1s, performance reviews, promotions, and performance improvement plans where needed.

 - Build and develop a leadership bench by coaching senior team members to run quality, coaching, and daily operations with increasing independence.

 - Set clear goals and expectations, and keep every team member connected to their impact on customers and company outcomes.

 - Build a culture of direct, kind feedback, ownership, and continuous learning.

 - Own team health: workload, engagement, retention, and sustainable coverage.


OWN THE STRATEGY, STANDARDS, AND RESULTS OF PRODUCT SUPPORT

 - Define and execute the Product Support strategy, roadmap, and operating plan in line with company goals.

 - Own team targets for SLAs, quality, CSAT, first-contact resolution, and cost-to-serve, and report on them to senior leadership.

 - Set the quality bar: own the QA program, calibration practices, and coaching frameworks used across the team.

 - Plan headcount, capacity, and hiring against product launches, customer growth, and seasonal demand.

 - Build business cases for investment in people, tooling, and process.


SCALE THROUGH PROCESS, TOOLING, AND AI

 - Own the support operating model: queue management, routing, escalation paths, approval-gated workflows, and cross-channel and bilingual coverage.

 - Lead our AI-first approach to support. Identify, pilot, and roll out automation and AI assistants that improve quality and efficiency without compromising the customer experience.

 - Serve as the business owner for key support tools (such as Zendesk, phone/IVR, AI assistants, and analytics platforms) and administer them.

 - Make sure playbooks, macros, and internal documentation are accurate, current, and used.

 - Define how the team measures itself. Build the dashboards, reporting cadence, and review rhythms that drive decisions.


INCIDENT MANAGEMENT AND COMMUNICATIONS

 - Own Product Support's role in incident response for customer-impacting issues, and make sure a clear, practised process exists.

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, Risk & Compliance, and Customer Success on incident coordination, and ensure customer and internal communications are timely, accurate, and empathetic.

 - Lead post-incident reviews and drive the follow-up actions that prevent repeat issues.


BE THE VOICE OF THE CUSTOMER

 - Turn case data, contact drivers, and frontline insight into clear recommendations for Product, Engineering, and GTM teams.

 - Represent Product Support in roadmap planning and cross-functional initiatives, and make sure changes are supportable and land smoothly.

 - Work with Product, Engineering, and the Help Centre content owner to keep the team and customers ready for releases.

 - Co-design customer journeys and handoffs with Customer Success Management and Customer Activation.


RISK, COMPLIANCE, AND CONTROLS

 - Own the control environment for approval-gated and sensitive support workflows, including who can approve what and how it is documented.

 - Partner with Risk & Compliance to keep security, privacy, and regulatory standards embedded in how the team works.

 - Act as an escalation point and approving authority for sensitive customer and account decisions.


STAY CLOSE TO CUSTOMERS

 - Handle high-visibility escalations and executive-level customer conversations.

 - Step into the queue during spikes, launches, and incidents to stay close to the work and the product.




YOU'LL BE GREAT IN THIS ROLE IF: 

 - You've led support teams. You have 7+ years of experience in technical support, digital customer service, or IT help desk roles, including 2+ years managing people, ideally including managers or team leads. SaaS or fintech experience is highly preferred but not mandatory.

 - You develop leaders. You hire well, coach well, and move people along when it's time. You have given hard feedback, run performance processes, and built teams that outlast any single person.

 - You think in systems. You design operating models, not just queues. You see patterns, build frameworks, and turn one-off fixes into durable improvements.

 - You're data-driven. You use metrics to set targets, prioritize work, forecast capacity, and tell a clear story to senior leaders and cross-functional partners.

 - You're AI-first. You have an opinion on where automation and AI help support and where they don't, and you have shipped changes that proved it.

 - You communicate with clarity and empathy. You translate complex problems for customers, teammates, and executives, and you know when to escalate.

 - You're a strong cross-functional partner. You build trust with Product, Engineering, Risk & Compliance, RevOps, and Customer Success, and you influence without relying on authority.

 - You're calm in an incident. You bring structure, clear communication, and ownership when things break.

 - You're an owner. You don't wait to be told what's broken. You hold yourself accountable to outcomes, not just activity.

 - You're flexible and reliable. Support needs can shift quickly. You're willing to adjust your schedule, jump into the queue during spikes, and support evenings or weekends on occasion.




THIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF: 

 - You aren't prepared to be in our downtown Toronto office 2-3 days a week.

 - You aren't prepared to always provide exceptional customer experiences.

 - You aren't passionate about helping Float build the best corporate card and spend management platform in Canada.

 - You aren't ready to embrace an AI-first approach.

 - You need a playbook of answers for every problem.

 - You love routine and a predictable day-to-day schedule.

 - You aren't adaptable to change or pivoting on the fly.

 - You prefer a slow pace and aren't an "all in" person.

 - You aren't able to manage multiple priorities at once.




WHY YOU SHOULD JOIN

IN SHORT

At Float, you'll thrive if you're bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special—and having a lot of fun along the way. If you're excited to build, grow, and win together, we'd love to meet you.

About KidKare 
 The people who care for and feed children every day have enough on their plates. Their software shouldn't add to it. 
 For more than 30 years, KidKare has built technology for the people behind childcare and child nutrition, helping them spend less time on paperwork, compliance, and administrative work and more time focused on the children and communities they serve.
 Our roots run deep in the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), a federal nutrition program that helps provide healthy meals and snacks to children and adults across the country. Today, we're building on that expertise with a growing ecosystem of software supporting childcare organizations across food program compliance, business management, professional development, and licensing.
 We're growing into new products, new markets, and have a much bigger vision for what KidKare can do for the childcare community. To support these goals, we're looking for a Product Growth Marketing Manager, Lifecycle & GTM Systems to build and run the engine that turns our product value into pipeline, adoption, and revenue.
 Position Summary 
 This is an execution-first growth role.
 You'll partner with Product and Revenue Operations leadership to define the positioning and value proposition for each product, then put them to work: translating individual product propositions and features into audience-specific messaging and deploying that messaging through various tactics. You’ll be involved in managing the CRM, data enrichment, prospect scoring, routing, & lifecycle marketing. You'll report to our VP of Revenue Operations and work across Product, Sales, and Customer Growth to turn every launch and feature release into measurable pipeline, adoption, and expansion.
 In a given week you might ship a new CRM workflow, tune a fit-and-intent scoring model, launch a demand-gen test to a newly enriched segment, build an app telemtry guide for a feature release, fix a routing rule that's sending leads to the wrong queue, or walk leadership through what moved in the funnel and why.
 You'll build the machine, and you'll run it. 
 You'll partner closely with our Digital Marketing Manager, who owns brand, creative, content, and channel execution. You'll own the systems, segmentation, lifecycle logic, experiment design, and measurement that make that work reach the right audience at the right moment. Together, you'll turn product and market insight into demand.
 Primary Responsibilities 
 Positioning, Feature Messaging & Launch Execution 
 •    Partner with product leadership to define and refine positioning and value propositions for each product and major release, grounded in customer, competitive, and market insight.
 •    Translate individual product features and releases into audience-specific messaging (the value, the proof, and the call to action) for each persona and segment we serve, carrying positioning down to the feature level.
 •    Execute launches through the systems you manage: target segments, lifecycle and nurture workflows, in-app guides, sales sequences and snippets, with launch tiers matched to the size of the release.
 •    Package features into the battlecards, talk tracks, and objection handling our Sales and Customer Growth teams need, delivered inside CRM where reps actually work.
 CRM Management & GTM Systems 
 •    Manage the CRM as the system of record for marketing and lifecycle: data model, custom properties, lifecycle stages, lead status, lists and segments, forms, and workflow automation.
 •    Maintain CRM data quality and governance, including deduplication, field standards, consistent deal stages across pipelines, and clear documentation, so Sales, Customer Growth, and leadership trust the data.
 •    Orchestrate the GTM stack (CRM, app telemtry, data enrichment, and automation tools) so product, marketing, and sales data flow cleanly between systems.
 Enrichment, AI Scoring & Routing 
 •    Build and maintain enrichment workflows that close firmographic, contact, and segment data gaps, including vertical-specific sources relating to childcare, education, and food program participation data.
 •    Design, deploy, and continuously tune fit, intent, and product-usage scoring models, using AI and predictive approaches where they outperform rules-based logic.
 •    Own lead and account routing rules, handoff SLAs, and alerts to Sales and Customer Growth, and monitor speed-to-lead and conversion by route.
 Demand Generation Experiments 
 •    Run a structured demand-gen experimentation program: define the hypothesis, audience, channel, offer, success metric, and decision rule before launch, then scale or move to the next experiment based on results.
 •    Build and execute campaigns, nurture tracks, and outbound sequences against enriched, scored segments, partnering with the Digital Marketing Manager on creative and channel execution.
 •    Use customer, competitive, and market insight to surface new segments and opportunities worth testing, and maintain a prioritized backlog and a visible results log so learnings compound.
 Lifecycle & In-App Engagement 
 •    Own lifecycle programs across the customer journey: onboarding, activation, feature adoption, cross-sell and expansion, renewal, and win-back.
 •    Build behavior-triggered journeys that combine CRM email and telemetry in-app guides, driven by product usage signals rather than calendar cadence alone.
 •    Partner with Product and Customer Growth to identify adoption gaps and cross-sell opportunities across our product portfolio, and run the programs that close them.
 Funnel Reporting & Measurement 
 •    Support maintenance of funnel stage definitions and conversion logic from first touch through closed-won, activation, and expansion.
 •    Build and own dashboards and recurring funnel reporting for RevOps and leadership, covering pipeline, conversion rates, velocity, channel and campaign performance, and product adoption.
 •    Set attribution and experiment measurement standards, and translate the numbers into clear recommendations on where to invest next. We care about great marketing, but ultimately we care about whether it drives growth.
 What Success Looks Like 
 •    First 90 days: You've aligned with product leadership on positioning for priority products; audited HubSpot data, lifecycle stages, and routing; published agreed funnel definitions; shipped a baseline funnel dashboard; and launched your first experiments.
 •    First 6 months: Enrichment and scoring are live and routing leads to Sales and Customer Growth against defined SLAs; core onboarding and adoption journeys are running across email and in-app; and experiments ship on a steady cadence with documented results.
 •    First 12 months: Every feature release runs through a repeatable launch playbook executed in the stack; conversion, speed-to-lead, and product adoption show measurable lift; and leadership uses your funnel reporting to make investment decisions.
 You'll Probably Love This Role If… 
 •    You're a builder who loves making the machine work, not just drawing the diagram. You'd rather ship the test than debate it.
 •    You're curious about customers, competitors, and markets and naturally find yourself asking, “Where's the opportunity here?”
 •    You read a feature release and immediately think about the segment, the trigger, the channel, and the metric.
 •    Messy CRM data bothers you, and you'd rather fix it at the source than patch it in a spreadsheet.
 •    You think in funnels and can explain, in plain language, why a conversion rate moved.
 •    You use AI as a force multiplier in real workflows, from enrichment and scoring to research and content variants, and you know where it helps and where it doesn't.
 •    You’re a natural collaborative and aren’t afraid to step outside of the RevOps team to work with Product, Sales, Customer Growth, and leadership. 
 •    You're comfortable owning your work end to end without needing a huge team around you.
 •    You're excited to build the GTM engine rather than inherit a finished one.
 Required Qualifications 
 •    4+ years in growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, marketing operations, revenue operations, or GTM engineering or a related B2B SaaS role.
 •    Hands-on CRM management/ownership as an admin or power user, including properties, lifecycle stages, workflows, lists, scoring, and reporting.
 •    Experience partnering with product leadership to define positioning and value propositions, and a proven ability to translate individual features into audience-specific messaging deployed across campaigns, lifecycle programs, in-app experiences, and sales enablement.
 •    Experience building data enrichment, lead scoring, and routing, including AI or predictive scoring approaches.
 •    A track record of designing and running demand-gen experiments with clear hypotheses, success metrics, and documented outcomes.
 •    Experience building behavior-triggered lifecycle programs across email and in-app channels.
 •    Strong funnel reporting and analytics skills: defining stages and conversion metrics, building dashboards, and working comfortably with data in spreadsheets or BI tools.
 •    Clear, concise writing, from lifecycle copy to experiment readouts to leadership summaries.
 •    Strong project management and systems thinking, with a habit of documenting what you build.
 •    A builder mentality and the ability to move comfortably between strategy and hands-on execution.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with CACFP, childcare, child nutrition, education, government programs, or other regulated industries is a huge plus, but not a requirement.
 CACFP has its own language, regulations, acronyms, and complexities. If you already know it, amazing. If you don't, you'll be surrounded by an exceptional team of people who do, and we'll help you get up to speed.
 A few other things we'd love to see:
 •    Experience with vertical SaaS, multi-product portfolios, or marketing to both SMB and enterprise or public-sector buyers.
 •    CRM certifications (Marketing, Sales, or Operations related) or hands-on experience with CRM AI and data enrichment features.
 •    Hands-on experience with in-app engagement or product adoption platforms
 •    Experience with enrichment and GTM automation tools
 •    Technical comfort beyond the UI: SQL, APIs and webhooks, or light scripting (JavaScript or Python) to connect systems and automate workflows.
 •    Comfort building AI-powered workflows for research, enrichment, scoring, and content variation. You know how to make AI your copilot, not your copywriter.
 Why KidKare? 
 We're at an exciting inflection point, taking decades of experience in childcare and child nutrition and using it to build a broader ecosystem of products for the organizations and people who help care for our communities.
 You won't be starting from scratch. We've invested deeply in understanding our customers, markets, competitors, and products. But we're not handing you a finished machine and asking you to keep it running.
 We want you to build the engine that powers what comes next. 
 If you want to own the systems, run the experiments, build the lifecycle, measure the funnel, and see exactly how your work moves pipeline and adoption, you'll have plenty to dig into here.
 All qualified applicants will be afforded equal employment opportunities without discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or marital status.

The Role   
 At Treewalk, you’ll own the entire public-company reporting cycle: fast closes, MD&A storytelling, IFRS/US GAAP judgment calls, and scalable system design. You’ll own end-to-end financial disclosure for a portfolio of high growth clients in technology, including fintech, software developers, quantum computing, and SaaS reporting issuers. Many engagements will tap you as a de-facto fractional CFO, guiding strategy as well as disclosure; others will lean on you as the go-to technical expert. Either way, every file is yours to run. 
 Deadlines are real; overtime isn’t a lifestyle. We staff sensibly, treat extra hours as the rare exception, and back that up with true schedule autonomy and remote flexibility—so your evenings stay yours. 
 If you’ve led pub-co audits at a small- to mid-size firm or managed reporting inside a listed issuer, and you’re ready to trade 70-hour busy-season marathons for high-impact work, tangible ownership, and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you. 
 How You’ll Create Impact Day-to-Day 
 Own the story behind the numbers: Draft and polish quarterly and annual financial statements and MD&A that stand up to capital-markets scrutiny and tell each client’s growth narrative.
 Master the technical hurdles: Tackle complex issues such as accounting for research and development expenses, revenue recognition, intangible assets and impairment, and package them into robust technical memos and disclosures.
 Untangle complex capital structures: Work through warrants, convertible instruments, derivative liabilities, unit offerings, debt/equity splits, and stock-based compensation.
 Run the engine of multi-entity groups: Build rock-solid consolidation and foreign-currency translation models that make complex structures look effortless.
 Turn data into insight: Deliver sharp balance sheet and P&L analyses, spotlighting trends and red-flag variances before anyone else sees them.
 Keep leadership laser-focused: Produce monthly variance reports against forecasts and annual plans, translating the findings into clear, action-ready recommendations, including cash runway and financing timing.
 Shape the roadmap: Guide annual budgets and rolling forecasts, aligning stakeholders around targets that push the business without breaking it.
 Step in as the “extra brain”: Handle special-project bookkeeping or period-end close entries when clients need a fractional controller’s precision and speed.
 Make audits painless: Design year-end audit plans, prep airtight support, and quarterback conversations with external auditors so CEOs and CFOs can sleep at night.
 Guard continuous disclosure: Stay ahead of regulatory changes, draft timely filings, and ensure nothing slips through the cracks on SEDAR+ or EDGAR.
 Build and grow the industry service line: Take ownership of the practice area and scale it, and develop the people who will run alongside you. 
 Result: clients see you as the calm, expert voice who keeps them compliant and strategic, while you build Treewalk’s Technology service line without the grind of traditional public practice. 
 Our ideal candidate... 
 CPA designation required.
 Significant public company audit and/or financial reporting experience, serving or working within early-stage or scaling technology reporting issuers listed in Canada and/or the US.
 Hands-on technical accounting depth in technology, including SaaS and multiple-element revenue recognition, capitalized software development costs, and impairment models.
 After the base experience requirements are met, we hire first and foremost for strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Why Treewalk Feels Different 
 It’s Treewalk for a reason: we invest in your growth, trust your judgment, and protect your life outside the ledger.
 No-Strings Learning Fund: We pay 100% of your CPA modules, annual dues, and any pro-dev courses you choose, and we’ll never claw it back if you move on.
 Freedom Over Face-Time: Own your deadlines, shape your schedule. Hit a midday workout, do the school run. Just bring the results.
 Day-One Peace of Mind: Extended health, dental, vision, and parental-leave benefits start the moment you join.
 Who We Are 
 Treewalk is Vancouver-born, scaling nationwide, and obsessed with turning capital-markets complexity into clarity. We give TSX, TSX-V, CSE, NASDAQ, and OTC issuers an end-to-end disclosure engine, so they can focus on growth while we keep them bullet-proof in the spotlight.
 But labels like “accounting firm” don’t capture our DNA. Picture a tech startup powered by CPAs:
 Holacracy over hierarchy: Ideas outrank titles, and ownership lives on every desk.
 Sector depth, startup curiosity: If it’s innovative, we’re already in it, or will be tomorrow.
 Growth at warp speed: One of Canada’s fastest-rising advisory practices, we set audacious goals, then sprint past them.
 Training ground for tomorrow’s CFOs: Whether you’re a seasoned audit manager or a controller at a technology company, Treewalk is where accountants level up for industry roles and capital-markets strategy.
 The Values That Power Us 
 Mastery: We hunt knowledge relentlessly and build expertise into every engagement.
 Support: No one goes it alone. Collaboration is our default setting.
 Ownership: We celebrate wins and own slip-ups with equal conviction.
 Kaizen: Continuous improvement isn’t a buzzword; it’s our daily operating system.
 Annual Salary: $125,000
